"'''Lollipop'''" is a song by American rapper and singer [[Lil Wayne]] posthumously featuring fellow American singer [[Static Major]]. A [[dirty rap]] song with [[hip house]], [[Trap music|trap]] and [[R&B]] elements, it was released on March 13, 2008 as the [[lead single]] from the former's sixth studio album ''[[Tha Carter III]]''.<ref name="rapup">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080315020350/http://www.rap-up.com/2008/03/11/new-music-lil-wayne-f-static-lollipop/ New Music: Lil Wayne F/ Static – 'Lollipop']. Rap-Up (March 11, 2008). Accessed March 12, 2008.</ref> The track, which heavily utilizes the [[Auto-Tune]] vocal effect, was produced by American record producers [[Deezle]] and [[Jim Jonsin]] and features lyrics about [[sexual desire]] and [[oral sex]]. A remixed version with a guest appearance from American rapper [[Kanye West]], as well as featuring new verses from Lil Wayne, was released as a bonus track for the album on [[iTunes Store|iTunes]].<ref name=rapup />

"Lollipop" became the most successful song by both artists, as it spent five non-consecutive weeks atop the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref name=billboard>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121103214344/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/news/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003815868/ Lil Wayne Continues Hot 100 Dominance]. Billboard (June 12, 2008). Accessed June 13, 2008.</ref> Static Major died on February 25, 2008, approximately two weeks before the song's release, making it the eighth song to peak the chart after the death of a credited artist.<ref name=blender>Jonah Weiner (February 22, 2008). [http://www.blender.com/Exclusive-Previewing-Lil-Waynes-Tha-Carter-III/Blender-Blog/blogs/1168/18751.aspx Exclusive: Previewing Lil Wayne's Tha Carter III] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080226071122/http://www.blender.com/Exclusive-Previewing-Lil-Waynes-Tha-Carter-III/Blender-Blog/blogs/1168/18751.aspx |date=February 26, 2008 }}. ''Blender''. Accessed February 23, 2008.</ref> It received [[RIAA certification|diamond]] certification by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) for selling ten million units in the United States<ref>{{Certification Cite|region=United States|title=Lollipop|artist=Lil Wayne|type=single}}</ref> and was ranked the number one hip hop song of 2008 by [[MTV]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Reid |first=Shaheem |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1601236/20081212/lil_wayne.jhtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216170905/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1601236/20081212/lil_wayne.jhtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 16, 2008 |title=Lil Wayne's 'A Milli' And More Top Hip-Hop Songs Of 2008; 50 Cent Pledges Loyalty To Eminem: Mixtape Monday – Music, Celebrity, Artist News |publisher=MTV.com |date=December 15, 2008 |access-date=June 18, 2012}}</ref> The song reached number one on the 2008 issue of ''Notarized'' by [[BET]]. The song was ranked at number five on ''[[Rolling Stone]]''{{'}}s list of the 100 Best Songs of 2008.<ref>No byline (December 25, 2008). [https://web.archive.org/web/20081227111805/http://www.rollingstone.com/news/story/24947047/the_100_best_singles_of_2008 "The 100 Best Songs of 2007"] ''Rolling Stone'', Retrieved December 25, 2008</ref><!--Template:Rolling Stone's 100 Best Songs of 2008--> With 9.1 million copies sold as of January 2009, "Lollipop" was named 2008's best-selling digital single worldwide by [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry|IFPI]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ifpi.org/content/library/DMR2009-real.pdf |title=DIGITAL MUSIC REPORT 2009 |access-date=September 1, 2012|archive-date=March 31, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100331044030/http://www.ifpi.org/content/library/DMR2009-real.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

"Lollipop" is a song by American rapper and singer Lil Wayne posthumously featuring fellow American singer Static Major. A dirty rap song with hip house, trap and R&B elements, it was released on March 13, 2008 as the lead single from the former's sixth studio album Tha Carter III. The track, which heavily utilizes the Auto-Tune vocal effect, was produced by American record producers Deezle and Jim Jonsin and features lyrics about sexual desire and oral sex. A remixed version with a guest appearance from American rapper Kanye West, as well as featuring new verses from Lil Wayne, was released as a bonus track for the album on iTunes.

"Lollipop" became the most successful song by both artists, as it spent five non-consecutive weeks atop the US Billboard Hot 100. Static Major died on February 25, 2008, approximately two weeks before the song's release, making it the eighth song to peak the chart after the death of a credited artist. It received diamond certification by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for selling ten million units in the United States and was ranked the number one hip hop song of 2008 by MTV. The song reached number one on the 2008 issue of Notarized by BET. The song was ranked at number five on Rolling Stone{{'}}s list of the 100 Best Songs of 2008. With 9.1 million copies sold as of January 2009, "Lollipop" was named 2008's best-selling digital single worldwide by IFPI.

The [[music video]] for the song was directed by [[Gil Green (director)|Gil Green]] and filmed in [[Las Vegas Valley|Las Vegas]] at Gavin Maloof's residence on December 31, 2007. He also filmed at 1700 East Flamingo Road in Las Vegas.<ref>Mariel Conception (February 2, 2008). [http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1046670/lil-wayne-new-album-will-stick-with-you-forever Lil Wayne: New Album 'Will Stick With You Forever']. ''Billboard''. Accessed February 2, 2008.</ref><ref>Andreas Hale (February 2, 2008). [http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.6313/title.lil-wayne-speaks-since-arrest Lil Wayne Speaks Since Arrest]. HipHopDX. Accessed February 2, 2008.</ref> The video premiered via [[Black Entertainment Television|BET]]'s ''Access Granted'' on March 12, 2008. It also reached number one on ''[[Total Request Live|TRL]]'' in April on [[MTV]].

The limousine that Wayne and Static get into at the start of the video is based on an [[International XT]] pickup truck.

The video is the most-viewed video on [[Music Choice]]'s [[video on demand]] service.<ref name="auto">[http://www.marketwatch.com/news/story/universal-music-group-music-choice/story.aspx?guid=%7BF1C3B37B-6A26-4AAC-BBA5-806AB322DAD1%7D&dist=hppr]  {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080811054803/http://www.marketwatch.com/news/story/universal-music-group-music-choice/story.aspx?guid=%7BF1C3B37B-6A26-4AAC-BBA5-806AB322DAD1%7D&dist=hppr|date=August 11, 2008}}</ref>

[[Jim Jonsin]], [[Tyga]], [[Jay Rock]], [[Birdman (rapper)|Birdman]] and [[Mack 10]] make cameos in the video.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-17 |title=The Number Ones: Lil Wayne's "Lollipop" (Feat. Static Major) |url=https://stereogum.com/2219481/the-number-ones-lil-waynes-lollipop-feat-static-major/columns/the-number-ones/ |access-date=2026-06-12 |website=stereogum.com |language=en}}</ref>

The final frame of the video is a picture of Static praying with the words "In memory of Stephen "Static Major" Garrett".

The music video for the song was directed by Gil Green and filmed in Las Vegas at Gavin Maloof's residence on December 31, 2007. He also filmed at 1700 East Flamingo Road in Las Vegas. The video premiered via BET's Access Granted on March 12, 2008. It also reached number one on TRL in April on MTV.

The limousine that Wayne and Static get into at the start of the video is based on an International XT pickup truck.

The video is the most-viewed video on Music Choice's video on demand service.

Jim Jonsin, Tyga, Jay Rock, Birdman and Mack 10 make cameos in the video.

The final frame of the video is a picture of Static praying with the words "In memory of Stephen "Static Major" Garrett".

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
The song won a [[Grammy Award]] at the [[51st Annual Grammy Awards]] for [[Grammy Award for Best Rap Song|Best Rap Song]].

Static Major died unexpectedly during a medical procedure on February 25, 2008, sixteen days before the song was released. "Lollipop" jumped 76 spots from number 85 to number 9 on the March 28, 2008 issue of the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming Lil' Wayne's highest-charting single as a lead artist, along with being his first top ten hit on the chart as a lead artist. His previous highest-charting position as a lead artist was with "[[Go D.J.]]", which peaked at number 14 in 2004. The following week, it reached a new peak of number 7 on the Hot 100. The single reached a new peak of number 2 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 on April 17, 2008, making it his highest-charting single as both a lead artist or as a featured performer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/chart_display.jsp?g=Singles&f=The+Billboard+Hot+100 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051101065317/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/chart_display.jsp?g=Singles&f=The+Billboard+Hot+100 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 1, 2005 |title=Billboard Hot 100 Music Charts -Most Trusted Music Charts in the Industry |language=fr |publisher=Billboard.com |access-date=June 18, 2012}}</ref> (Lil Wayne was a featured artist for [[Destiny's Child]]'s number 3 (Hot 100) hit, "[[Soldier (Destiny's Child song)|Soldier]]".) For the week of May 3, 2008, "Lollipop" reached the number-one spot on the Hot 100, his first number one on the chart. It is also Wayne's first number one on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] chart and the [[Hot Rap Songs|Hot Rap Tracks]] chart. On the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, it is the first rap song to reach number one since [[Ludacris]]' "[[Money Maker]]" in 2006. After one week, it slipped away from top spot, but returned three weeks later, making it the song with the longest break in between peaks in the Hot 100 since [[Usher (singer)|Usher]]'s "[[U Got It Bad]]."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/news/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003797323|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080502060746/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/news/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003797323|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 2, 2008|title=Leona Lewis Regains No. 1 On Hot 100| magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date=May 2, 2008|access-date=July 11, 2018}}</ref>

The week after the release, Wayne and [[Mariah Carey]] became the number one most added and greatest gainer at both radio formats with a total of 138 adds.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.djbooth.net/index/news/entry/lil-waynes-lollipop-makes-radio-history-03270811/ |title="Lil' Wayne's "Lollipop" Makes Radio History" - March 27, 2008 |newspaper=Djbooth |publisher=DJBooth.net |date=March 27, 2008 |access-date=June 18, 2012}}</ref> "Lollipop" has become a crossover hit on mainstream radio, as it became his first top 40 hit as a lead artist, entering at number 36, and has so far peaked at number 5.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://w2.mediabase.com/mmrweb/AllAccess/Charts.asp?format=h1r&showtopn=500&cutoff=1 |title=Mediabase 24/7 - 7 Day Charts |website=w2.mediabase.com |access-date=14 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071029212637/http://w2.mediabase.com/mmrweb/AllAccess/Charts.asp?format=h1r&showtopn=500&cutoff=1 |archive-date=29 October 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> It is his first top ten on the [[Pop 100]], where it has reached number two. It returned to number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 for the second time on May 22, 2008.

The song has become a top ten success in Canada, peaking at number 10 as of May 29, 2008, and his most successful song in the UK, where it reached number 26 on downloads alone. It reached number 3 on the New Zealand charts and was certified double Platinum by the [[Recorded Music NZ|Recording Industry Association of New Zealand]].<ref name=NZcert/>

In 2008, "Lollipop" was the best-selling ringtone in the [[United States]] with over 2.3 million copies sold<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.yorapper.com/lil-waynes-lollipop-highest-selling-ringtone-for-2008/ |title=Lil Wayne's "Lollipop" Highest Selling Ringtone for 2008 |publisher=Yorapper.com |date=January 10, 2009 |access-date=June 18, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.egradioonline.com/2009/01/2008-top-selling-hip-hopr-artists_02.html |title=2008 Top Selling Hip Hop/R&B Artists, Ringtones, and Albums |publisher=E.G Radio Online |access-date=June 18, 2012 |archive-date=December 20, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220030412/http://www.egradioonline.com/2009/01/2008-top-selling-hip-hopr-artists_02.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the second best-selling digital song with over 3.1 million copies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.businesswire.com/portal/site/home/permalink/?ndmViewId=news_view&newsId=20081231005304&newsLang=en |title=2008 U.S. Music Purchases Exceed 1.5 Billion; Growth in Overall Music Purchases Exceeds 10% |publisher=Business Wire |date=December 31, 2008 |access-date=June 18, 2012}}</ref>

To date, "Lollipop" sold 4,176,000 digital copies in the United States.<ref>{{cite web|last=Grein |first=Paul |url=http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/74360/week-ending-may-1-2011-songs-even-divas-struggle/;_ylt=Aieo0d1IfEz.YSYE4keHbBwPwiUv |title=Week Ending May 1, 2011. Songs: Even Divas Struggle | Chart Watch – Yahoo! Music |publisher=New.music.yahoo.com |date=May 4, 2011 |access-date=June 18, 2012}}</ref>

sections.heading: Remixes and covers
sections.wikitext:
The song was officially [[remix]]ed featuring vocals from Static Major and a verse from American rapper [[Kanye West]]. There is an extended version of the remix that has Wayne talking over the original bridge and singing an altered hook, with West singing adlibs, along with a guitar solo near the end. Other remixes feature [[Young Jeezy]], [[Gorilla Zoe]], [[Ace Hood]], [[Kurupt]], [[V.I.C. (rapper)|V.I.C.]], [[Nicki Minaj]], [[Wiz Khalifa]], [[Teki Latex|Tekitek]], [[Rasheeda]] and [[Khia]], who made a popular female version of the song.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://allnumberoneradio-kxklhd.itmblog.com/2009/02/23/the-top-20-songs-of-2008-on-the-billboard-hot-100/ |title=The Top 20 Songs of 2008 on the Billboard Hot 100 |publisher=Allnumberoneradio-kxklhd.itmblog.com |access-date=June 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100324011418/http://allnumberoneradio-kxklhd.itmblog.com/2009/02/23/the-top-20-songs-of-2008-on-the-billboard-hot-100/ |archive-date=March 24, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Another remix was made commemorating the 2008 NBA champion [[Boston Celtics]]. It features the instrumental used in the main song.

[[David Banner]]'s song "[[Shawty Say]]" samples the opening part of the Lil Wayne's second verse for its chorus. [[JJ (Swedish band)|JJ]] uses elements of "Lollipop" in their song "[[jj n° 2|Ecstasy]]". Wayne's protégé [[Drake (musician)|Drake]] samples this song on his song "[[In My Feelings]]" from his fifth studio album, ''[[Scorpion (Drake album)|Scorpion]]''.

The song was officially remixed featuring vocals from Static Major and a verse from American rapper Kanye West. There is an extended version of the remix that has Wayne talking over the original bridge and singing an altered hook, with West singing adlibs, along with a guitar solo near the end. Other remixes feature Young Jeezy, Gorilla Zoe, Ace Hood, Kurupt, V.I.C., Nicki Minaj, Wiz Khalifa, Tekitek, Rasheeda and Khia, who made a popular female version of the song. Another remix was made commemorating the 2008 NBA champion Boston Celtics. It features the instrumental used in the main song.

David Banner's song "Shawty Say" samples the opening part of the Lil Wayne's second verse for its chorus. JJ uses elements of "Lollipop" in their song "Ecstasy". Wayne's protégé Drake samples this song on his song "In My Feelings" from his fifth studio album, Scorpion.

sections.wikitext:
{{Infobox song | name = Lollipop | cover = File-Framing Hanley - Lollipop.jpg | alt = | type = single | artist = [[Framing Hanley]] | album = [[The Moment (Framing Hanley album)|The Moment]] | released = 2008 | recorded = 2008 | studio = | venue = | genre = {{hlist|[[Hard rock]]|[[alternative rock]]}} | length = 3:07 | label = {{hlist|[[Silent Majority Group|Silent Majority]]|[[Universal Music Group|Universal]]}} | writer = {{hlist|Dwayne Carter|Stephen Garrett|Darius Harrison|Jim Jonsin|Rex Zamor}} | producer = Framing Hanley | prev_title = Hear Me Now | prev_year = 2007 | next_title = Hear Me Now (re-release) | next_year = 2009 }} The [[post-hardcore]] band [[Framing Hanley]] covered the song as a bonus track on their album ''[[The Moment (Framing Hanley album)|The Moment]]''.
